stances_toward.note: The only open, friendly border: a gas-for-electricity swap extended to 2030 (Aug 2023) and a roadmap of July 2026 (grid integration, Meghri hydropower, a rebuilt barter mechanism), the 400 kV Armenia-Iran line, a second bridge at Meghri-Nordooz and the Iranian-built Kajaran-Agarak road of the North-South corridor. Foreign minister Mirzoyan met Pezeshkian and Ghalibaf in Tehran on 6 Oct 2026; Iran says it is 'satisfied' with TRIPP, (the Iranian reaction to an American-run route on its border is a point to watch). Partner, no alliance: ties are pure interest, and Iran's own exposure to US pressure limits what Yerevan can build on it.

stances_toward.note: Competing interests and open friction, but no will to destroy the other: Baku accuses Iran of the Nakhchivan drone strike of 5 Mar 2026 (Aliyev demanded an apology and accountability, pulled diplomats from Tehran and Tabriz on 6 Mar, the security service reported foiled IRGC-linked plots against the BTC pipeline) while still meeting Pezeshkian in Bishkek on 31 Aug 2026 and hosting an Iranian military delegation at ADEX on 30 Sep 2026. Grievances: Iran's Armenia alignment, Azeri irredentism in both directions, Baku's Israeli ties. Not 'adversary': both sides keep talking and Baku refuses to host operations against Iran.

stances_toward.note: The rival-partner pair the brief describes, graded by its competitive side: the two compete for influence in Iraq, Syria and the Caucasus, and in the US-Israeli war on Iran of 2026 Ankara condemned the attack as a breach of international law, closed its airspace to US forces and sent condolences on Khamenei's death, but also criticised Iran's strikes on Gulf states, blamed Tehran for the failure of pre-war talks, and had three Iranian missiles intercepted over its territory by NATO (Iran denied targeting Turkey). It is also Iran's go-between (contacts with Washington, Pakistan and Qatar; offer to demine Hormuz). Stable because both sides want the border quiet. Not adversary: no declared aim against the Iranian regime. The 2025 Israel-Iran exchange in the brief is outside this source set. Bond - none.
